questions.question: The srcset attribute lets the browser:

options.text: Choose the best image source from a list based on screen density/size

questions.explanation: srcset provides candidate URLs with width (w) or density (x) descriptors; the browser picks the optimal one.

questions.question: The 'sizes' attribute tells the browser:

options.text: How much layout space the image will occupy, so it can pick the right srcset candidate
The number of images to load

questions.explanation: sizes describes rendered width (e.g. '(max-width:600px) 100vw, 50vw'), letting the browser select the correct srcset source.

questions.question: For 'art direction' (different crop or composition at different widths) you use:
questions.explanation: lets you serve entirely different images per media condition (art direction), with as the fallback.

questions.question: To enable native lazy-loading you add:
questions.explanation: loading="lazy" defers offscreen images until near viewport, improving initial load. Use loading="eager" for above-the-fold.

questions.question: Specifying width and height attributes on helps:

options.text: Reserve space and reduce layout shift (CLS)

questions.explanation: Known dimensions let the browser reserve aspect-ratio space, preventing Cumulative Layout Shift (a Core Web Vital).

questions.question: A modern format fallback strategy uses:
questions.explanation: Serve WebP/AVIF via with a universally-supported fallback for older browsers.

questions.question: x-descriptors in srcset (e.g. image.jpg 2x) describe:

options.text: Device pixel density (DPR) the candidate is intended for

questions.explanation: 1x/2x/3x tell the browser which source matches the device pixel ratio (retina). w-descriptors pair with sizes instead.

questions.question: Providing a descriptive alt attribute is important because:

options.text: It aids accessibility AND can appear if the image fails to load
It is required for srcset to work

questions.explanation: alt supports screen readers and shows as broken-image text; decorative images should use alt="".
